questions.stem: A project board runs `select p from Project p join fetch p.tasks order by p.id` with Hibernate 6. The database holds 12 projects; 2 of them have no tasks yet, and the other 10 have 40 tasks between them. What does the query return?

options.text: 12 projects from one statement, since the fetch fills each task list and leaves 2 of them empty
options.says: join fetch is an inner join, so a project with no task has no row in the result and isn't returned

options.text: 10 projects from one statement, since the join returns no row for a project without tasks
options.says: the inner join drops parents without children; left join fetch keeps them

options.text: 12 projects from 13 statements, since the fetch runs one task query for each project returned
options.says: join fetch loads the collection in the same statement as the parents: one statement

options.text: 10 projects from 11 statements, since the join drops 2 projects and then loads tasks per project
options.says: join fetch loads the collection in the same statement as the parents, so no per-project query follows

origin.section: A Lazy Association Costs One Query per Parent Unless the Query Fetches It

questions.stem: A pricing job opens one EntityManager at start-up and keeps it. It has already loaded product 7 at 19.90. An admin tool, using its own connection, sets product 7 to 24.90 and commits. The job then runs `select p from Product p where p.id = 7`. What does it get?

options.text: 24.90, with no statement sent, since the admin tool's commit updated the object the job holds
options.says: a commit through another connection changes the row, not objects held by another persistence context

options.text: 19.90, with one statement sent, since the query read the row and returned the held object unchanged
options.says: the query ran (one statement) and returned the instance already held for id 7, with its old state, until refresh() or clear()

options.text: 24.90, with one statement sent, since the query read the row and copied it onto the held object
options.says: Hibernate doesn't overwrite a managed object's state with a re-read row; only refresh() does

options.text: 19.90, with no statement sent, since the query was answered from the job's persistence context
options.says: a JPQL query always runs its SQL; only find() for a held id is answered from the context

origin.section: One Persistence Context Holds One Object per Row

questions.stem: A controller receives an `Order` that was loaded in an earlier request, whose EntityManager is closed. It sets `order.status = SHIPPED`, then in a new transaction calls `Order saved = em.merge(order);`, then sets `order.note = "left at door"`, and commits. What does the row hold after the commit?

options.text: SHIPPED and the new note, since merge kept the order's state in order and made order the tracked object
options.says: merge returns a managed copy; the object passed in stays detached, so the note set on it afterwards isn't checked

options.text: The old status and the new note, since merge copied the row into order and made order the tracked object
options.says: merge copies the detached object's state onto the managed copy, not the row onto the detached object, and order stays untracked

options.text: SHIPPED and the old note, since merge copied the order's state into saved and made saved the tracked object
options.says: merge copied the detached state (with SHIPPED) onto the managed copy it returned; the note set on the detached order after that is lost

options.text: The old status and the old note, since merge copied the row into saved and made saved the tracked object
options.says: merge copies the detached object's state, including changes made while detached, onto the managed copy, so SHIPPED is written at flush

origin.section: Only Managed Objects Are Checked, and merge Returns a Different One

questions.stem: A service method finds a `Customer` with `em.find`, closes its EntityManager and returns the customer. `addresses` is a `@OneToMany` with no fetch attribute, and the method never touched it. The view then loops over `customer.addresses`. Which describes what happens?

options.text: find loaded the addresses before the EntityManager closed, so the loop reads them
options.says: a @OneToMany is LAZY by default, so find left the collection unloaded

options.text: find loaded the addresses before the EntityManager closed, so the loop throws on them
options.says: a collection loaded before the context closed stays readable afterwards: the page's fetched collection gave 3 after close

options.text: find left the addresses unloaded when the EntityManager closed, so the loop reads none
options.says: Hibernate throws instead of returning an empty collection, which would read as a customer with no addresses

options.text: find left the addresses unloaded when the EntityManager closed, so the loop throws on them
options.says: LazyInitializationException: failed to lazily initialize a collection ... no Session; the context that could load them is closed

origin.section: A Lazy Association Loads Only While Its Persistence Context Is Open
